in_arabic.name: قُطب
in_arabic.long_meaning: قُطب هو مصطلح عربي يعني الزعيم أو القائد، ويُستخدم في الإسلام لوصف شخص يمتلك صفات قيادية وروحية عالية، وقد استخدم هذا المصطلح في التاريخ الإسلامي لوصف أعلام الدين والقادة الروحيين، وله أهمية كبيرة في الثقافة الإسلامية

in_urdu.name: قطب

data.cultural_impact: In Islamic architecture, the word qutub is used to describe a monumental pillar that often forms the central point, both structurally and symbolically, around which a mosque or mausoleum is built. These pillars have been instrumental in defining the aesthetic and architectural style of Islamic structures, and many famous mosques, such as the Qutub Minar in India, bear the name as a mark of their historical and cultural significance.
data.spiritual_significance: In a spiritual context, the term qutub holds deep significance as a symbol of stability, strength, and guidance. It is believed that God has appointed certain individuals as qutubs or spiritual leaders to guide humans on the path to spiritual growth and enlightenment. These individuals are considered to be the 'axes' around which their communities revolve, and their teachings and wisdom serve as a source of inspiration and support. Thus, the name 'Qutub' serves as a reminder of the essential role that spiritual leaders and pillars of faith play in our lives.
